97302085a4c9df62cc81980eab5d4814: Generation of Performance and Stress Tests from Functional Tests Although Software Testing is related to quality assurance, it demands time and resources, and therefore ends up not being carried out in part of the projects carried out. 5df7d1710bfe145bacb82ab64b238144: Implementation of Measurement in the Software Development Process – Experience Report and Lessons Learned Measurement is recognized as an important process to support software development management, but its effective implementation faces challenges related to the effort and knowledge required to generate useful information for decision making. 2d6afcd71abac69d859786a3bb7f3e42: Identification of Authorship of Manuscripts Based on Genetic and Generic Attributes of Writing Graphoscopy is an area of ​​forensic science dedicated, among other purposes, to the analysis and identification of the authorship of manuscripts, whether contemporary or ancient. dd3a7c531b5ecd8df3c4e281ef6498c4: Interactive Virtual Environment with Collision and Deformation of Objects for Medical Training Training in medical procedures can benefit from the use of interactive virtual environments that realistically simulate the user's actions. 8a791e0ed42dc52b7898a38bc98f8426: QOC*: using Design Rationale as a tool to manage knowledge in software projects During the development process of a software system, a large amount of knowledge is used and produced as a result of the options analyzed and the decisions made throughout the development of the project. 362ee8d132f8d8c4f5d0aeb3be040469: Use of the PreText tool to mine texts extracted from NCBI for the epistemological study of Health Informatics This article presents the use of the PreText tool as an auxiliary technique for research on the epistemology of Health Informatics (IS), which aims to infer whether IS is characterized as science, technology, technoscience or art. d130ac8142ac30af62a27e6af7f43fba: ALUPAS: Evaluation of performance and energy consumption of software for embedded systems With the proliferation of portable equipment operated by batteries, the design of low energy consumption embedded systems has aroused a lot of interest in recent years. 901c055bcd8afa67c9939842991d2985: Proactive Assessment of Deterioration of Information Systems through Management Measures Issues related to the modernization of information systems have received greater attention and relevance. 7a59bb56e98f6bda00f8b7e0c03210f9: Visual Effects, an Approach from Digital Image Processing This article introduces the most important concepts of digital imaging and discusses how they are used to create visual effects, and, at the same time, provides a panel of the various computer graphics and image processing techniques for cinema and video. 6a99a96a700142bda058fa202fef8cb8: Tutorial: Introduction to Computer Vision using OpenCV This tutorial presents introductory concepts of image processing (filters) and computer vision (segmentation, classification, pattern recognition and tracking). 9c99c77ec676a92ef7ddccd61956d11f: Analysis of Motor Control with Interactions using Conventional Devices and Augmented Reality This work presents software to help diagnose fine motor control problems in humans, called MOSKA (MOtor SKill Analyzer), using interaction techniques with conventional devices (based on devices such as mouse, graphics tablet - tablet) and Augmented Reality (AR) (based on low-cost devices such as webcam). 803820cd762552772b16a6a9a6e31dbc: Learning and Control of Autonomous Mobile Robots Using Visual Attention This paper describes a reinforcement learning model capable of learning complex control tasks using continuous actions and states. 9c4c5864630f521aa201747fab07260c: Policy Update Strategies for the Coordination of Swarm-Based Agents This article analyzes the influence of learning parameters of swarm algorithms and proposes policy update strategies generated by rewards (pheromones) for dynamic environments. Experimental results show that it is possible to accelerate the convergence to a consistent global policy, surpassing the results of classical swarm-based algorithmic approaches. 749531d4562cc0dd93b4c32f11dd9124: Estimation of Probability of Data Loss in Networks Using Multifractal Traffic Modeling and Many-Source Theory In this article, we propose an approach for estimating the probability of byte loss in computer network links considering multifractal properties of traffic flows. 1ec4f7e17b2c6b9d6ab57785584c30fc: Development and Evaluation of an Electronic Protocol for the Care and Monitoring of Patients with Celiac Disease This study aims to develop an electronic protocol with structured and specific information for the care and monitoring of patients with celiac disease, available on the web, and evaluate it in terms of usability. To evaluate the usability of the web system, the System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire was used. The SUS-score resulted in an average value of 83.5±10.0, which indicates that the web system was considered easy to use and in accordance with user satisfaction. The web system properly implemented the protocol. The use of the electronic protocol proved to be valid for the care and monitoring of patients with celiac disease, as it maintained the specificity of clinical data and the routine of the professionals involved. 00bb7bda886642a44d5a84b05c66f87b: Snake-3D in Three-Dimensional Modeling and Measurement of the Length of Electrical Arcs This work describes the unprecedented application of a three-dimensional active contour (snake-3D) in the evaluation of the length of electric arcs artificially generated in high voltage towers and captured through a pair of calibrated cameras. Asnake-3D is spatially represented by a B-spline that evolves under the constraints of forces external to the active contour and internal to it. External forces are obtained from pairs of images that capture the evolution of the electric arc, while internal forces are intrinsic to the active contour and determined by the voltage between adjacent control points. In relation to other approaches for recovering the 3D geometry of electric arcs, the model proposed here is independent of the determination of homologous points and specific camera positioning, in addition to providing tracking of the electric arc, taking into account the temporal dependence between consecutive pairs of frames in two videos. 788da7ab5688911bb36eda750fd51885: Aumento de Resolução Temporal de Sequências de Imagens do Trato Vocal por meio de Registro das Imagens O imageamento por ressonância magnética tem sido bastanteutilizado no estudo da produção da fala. Entretanto, é importante ressaltar que as resoluções espacial e temporal necessárias para a identificação do movimento dos articuladores da fala variam de acordo com a velocidade e localidade desse movimento, e tal informação não é conhecida a priori. Abordagens existentes procuram aprimorar a resolução das sequências de imagens melhorando o processo de aquisição ou utilizando meios de aquisição mais potentes, o que pode ser financeiramente inviável. O movimento identificado pelo registro permite o aumento de resolução temporal por meio de uma técnica de interpolação por compensação de movimento. 55791bd006a71bae30a9842fa5ed8c30: Impulsive Noise Elimination Using a Selective Median Filter and Isotropic Diffusion This work presents an algorithm combining a modification of the standard median filter, based on the impulsive noise detector proposed by Chen, Yang and Cao, with an isotropic diffusion process to remove salt and pepper noise. d0edf564d7a2d9b3cf9fe30f8594597a: Statistical Model for Determining the Optimal Number of Iterations of the Anisotropic Diffusion Filter Applied to Noise Reduction of Brain Magnetic Resonance Images Despite the great success of anisotropic diffusion filters in reducing noise in medical images, a limitation of this iterative approach is the automatic determination of the correct number of iterations of the algorithm, since a large number of iterations can cause excessive blurring of the edges between structures anatomical images, while a small number may not be enough to completely remove noise from the image. Therefore, this work proposes a statistical model for automatically determining the optimal number of iterations of the anisotropic diffusion filter applied to noise reduction in medical images. The model is determined "off-line" by maximizing the structural similarity index, which is used in this work as an objective function to quantitatively evaluate the quality of the resulting images after each filter iteration. e386e572007f5cdcafbb23868caa306c: Swarm Intelligence and Verhulst Equilibrium Applied to Power Allocation in Partitioned CDMA Optical Networks The use of the code division multiple access (CDMA) technique in purely optical networks was proposed taking into account their wide optical bandwidth. Optical CDMA is a technique that allows multiple users to simultaneously share the same fiber channel asynchronously without \textit{delay} and without the need for resource management (\textit{scheduling}). However, multiple access interference (MAI) levels are significant in these systems due to the nature of incoherent power detection. Reducing this interference effect is crucial in improving the performance of optical CDMA systems. In this sense, it is proposed to use resource allocation mechanisms, particularly power, that guarantee each user a minimum acceptable performance in terms of bit error rate (BER). In the centralized power control strategy, it is necessary that a central node has information about the gain of all links. In turn, in the partitioned power control (access network and \textit{broadcast} network) it is verified that the optical signals after the star coupler do not contribute to the determination of the MAI and therefore do not affect the power balance associated with each laser. In this work, the problem of power control for partitioned CDMA optical networks (p-OCDMA) is analyzed from two different points of view: a) Verhulst's mathematical model of population growth, discussed in [1]; b) heuristic approach called \emph{swarm} intelligence (PSO -- \textit{particle swarm optimization}). Extensive simulations and numerical results indicated that both the Verhulst model and the PSO are suitable for solving the problem of power control in p-OCDMA networks, from the point of view of uni-objective optimization, with satisfactory convergence results for a variety of operating scenarios for the p-OCDMA system. Finally, a complexity analysis in terms of number of operations is carried out in order to obtain a more realistic comparative picture for the two optimization methodologies, clearly indicating the superiority of the analytical-iterative approach of Verhulst's approach. Physics; Humanities; Mathematics; computer science; Philosophy
1559d72d9cfd34eafd4fb0c4f8df19e3: Integration of evidence in credal networks and Jeffrey's rule Credal networks provide a scheme for representing imprecise probabilistic models. These algorithms do not perform evidential reasoning in the case in which the evidence must be processed according to the conditioning rule proposed by R.C. Jeffrey. e086ad1ccadd9e77fb0621741b898fdd: A Framework for the Development of Formal Concept Analysis Algorithms This work presents a framework for the development of formal concept analysis (CFA) algorithms. Originally developed to serve as an instrument to aid in learning the main AFC algorithms, nothing prevents it from being used to evaluate new algorithms. 9a915a11aa0a5bd674b5b3746eee4d3c: Skew Detection in Document Images Scanning documents contributes to the preservation of information, preventing its loss due to physical degradation of the paper. Currently, Automatic Document Image Recognition Systems are used to automatically convert the information contained in images into editable text, quickly and without the need for an individual to be present. Thus, making this information searchable through, for example, keywords. Slanting in documents is a frequent problem in these systems and, in general, is imposed during scanning, when the paper is positioned at an angle other than zero degrees on the scanner axis. In the case of handwritten documents, slant can appear while writing the document itself, especially when the writer does not have an agenda line as a guide. Tilt correction is essential for the good performance of automatic recognition systems. This work addresses the problem of tilt detection in printed and handwritten documents, providing a review of the main methods for tilt detection published in the literature to date. The main techniques are exposed in a categorized way and advantages and limitations of each method are discussed. Physics; Humanities; art
4e7ee4f854ac4282c9f842fb236bff2b: Using CSP, RSL, and the PopOrg Model in the Formal Specification of MAS Organizations This article explores the use of traditional formal software engineering methods for the formal specification of multi-agent systems organizations. Several simulations were carried out to comparatively analyze the behaviors of different predator agents in two types of environments: with or without competition between predators. 782dca1263f4951761d6b9847d6b9322: Planning a Serious Games Aimed at Oral Health in Babies Serious games are computer games whose main characteristic is to teach specific aspects of disciplines or train operational and behavioral skills. e686184e8b04012c0b8f6eaccfb34484: Use of Random Walk in the Identification of Document Characteristics in the Portuguese Language Due to the large volume of stored texts, the text mining area has been the focus of numerous research aimed at the automatic classification of documents. d454b8e25b1b3ce590c9d4f6058672aa: An Open and Service-Oriented Architecture for Personal Assistant Software Several efforts have been made towards personal assistant software (SAP) with the aim of helping people in their daily activities, at home or at work. b9ae8c666ae8f9ed662963b02cd95310: A Systematic Review of Approaches in Virtual Organizations in the Context of Trust, Reputation and Cloud Computing Virtual Organizations represent a prominent form of collaboration in which a set of companies share skills, competencies and risks to meet a common objective. 65501c6e5670acad5d8f1af2b8a8c52a: Identification of seed samples using Computer Vision Several computer systems aimed at Agribusiness have been developed to improve productivity, product quality, reduce waste and assist in decision making. b35f96c1ba51de2e9fc95754248059f4: Performance analysis of Relational and Non-Relational Databases on genomic data The storage of genomic data is a major challenge today, as with the advancement of molecular technology the amount of genomic data generated is increasing, so that the sequencing of a single organism can generate files with gigabytes of information. In general, genomic data manipulation processes use simple files as the main means of storing such data. However, modern databases present themselves as an alternative for managing this data by offering better organization, fault tolerance, better use of available storage space and performance. Furthermore, databases make it possible to add meta-information about the stored DNA sequences to the raw sequencing data. Given this scenario, this work presents and evaluates the performance of different storage strategies in three databases belonging to two different paradigms, MySQL (representative of Relational databases), Cassandra and MongoDB (representative of Non-Relational databases). The results demonstrated that relational databases have limitations when they are inserted in an environment with large masses of data. Physics; Humanities; Philosophy
d72ef1cbf5901d588a6765d4c6e25554: Study and Modeling of the Effects of Shape and Growth in Coat Pattern Formation Processes via Reaction-Diffusion Reaction-diffusion models are widely used in the simulation of pattern formation in living beings, being applied both as an explanation of these phenomena and for the generation of textures in computer graphics. In this work, we performed simulations with Turing's nonlinear reaction-diffusion model on two-dimensional surfaces using different parameters and surface shapes. 9c9bcfe06130b2fcbbe3eb3fceb1a38c: Positioning of 3D Circuits Considering 3D-Vias Planning This work explores methods to perform the positioning of a particular type of VLSI circuits known as 3D circuit (three dimensions). Unlike previous works, this article addresses the problem of 3D positioning considering vertical connections (called 3D-Vias) and the limitations imposed by them. A complete positioning flow was carried out, starting with the treatment of input and output (I/O) pins and followed by global positioning, detailed positioning and 3D-Vias positioning. The first stage seeks to distribute the I/O pins in a balanced way, aiming to assist positioning to obtain a reduced number of 3D-Vias. The global positioning mechanism based on the Quadratic Placement algorithm considers information provided by manufacturing technology and 3D-Vias spacing requirement to reduce the length of connections and balance the distribution of cells in 3D. Critical connections can be addressed through the insertion of artificial networks that help prevent 3D-Vias from being used in their implementation. Finally, the 3D-Vias are positioned by a fast algorithm based on Tetris legalization. The complete framework reinforces the potential benefits of 3D circuits to reduce connection lengths and presents efficient algorithms designed for 3D circuits that can be incorporated into new CAD tools. f409fbcc76cbf9ad9fdc058783ad8b0c: Autonomous Investment Analysis: A Discrete Multi-Agent Approach Since the early days of computer science, researchers have wondered where the line is between the tasks that machines can do and those that only humans can perform. Several tasks were identified as impossible for machines and later conquered by new advances in Artificial Intelligence. Nowadays, it seems that we are not far from the day when driving cars will be included in the tasks that machines can do efficiently. Certainly, even more complex activities will be dominated by machines in the future. In this article, we argue that investment analysis, the process of evaluating and selecting investments in terms of risk and return, may be among the tasks performed efficiently by machines in the perhaps not distant future. In fact, there are significant research efforts to create algorithms and quantitative methods for analyzing investments. We present a brief review about them. Through this review, we can see that there are many challenges and complexities to be faced in the pursuit of autonomous investment analysis (AAI). In this article, we propose an approach to simplify the problem of autonomous investment analysis capable of dealing with the identified complexities (nature of assets, multiple analysis algorithms per asset, non-stationarity and multiple investment horizons). This approach is based on the simultaneous use of several autonomous agents and the discretization of the AAI problem and its modeling as a classification problem. This approach breaks down the complexity faced by AAI into problems that can be addressed by a group of agents working together to provide intelligent, personalized investment advice to individuals. We present an implementation of this approach and results obtained through its use with historical data from the Brazilian capital market. We believe that such an approach can contribute to the development of AAI. Furthermore, this approach allows the incorporation of already known algorithms and techniques that can help solve part of the problem. Philosophy; Humanities; Economics
74714ad169abe27be6a7f187f91ea561: Managing Changes to XML Documents XML documents are increasingly present in development projects, and are often placed in version control systems along with other project files. These systems do not consider the specific format of XML files, treating them as common text files. In this way, automatic merges can generate malformed documents silently, and display, during comparisons, changes that have no relevance to XML documents, often masking relevant changes. This article proposes an approach for displaying differences and supporting the merging of XML files, using classic algorithms proposed in the literature. The proposed approach allows the execution of changes in parallel in a more controlled, safe and efficient way for XML documents. Humanities; computer science; Physics; art
ca0a958e4434fbf8a779fadaa2bcb9bf: Strategies for Building Multi-Label Classifier Committees in Semi-Supervised Multi-Description Learning Multi-label classification is a supervised learning problem in which an object can be associated with multiple classes. 26f8342b46c26c147e99506c2e491845: Multi-agent Simulation of the Kiss Nightclub Evacuation: The Importance of NBR 9.077 and its relationship with the Panic This article uses the evacuation scenario of a tragedy involving the Kiss nightclub in 2013 in Southern Brazil. 5c3a3158bd58a26adb86bff0e31d1eeb: Composition of EBDI Agents: WASABI-Jason Integration Emotions play a very important role in the decision-making process of human beings and it is natural that their use becomes a very fertile field in the area of ​​Artificial Intelligence, whether with the aim of bringing the behavior of computational agents closer to that of humans, or simply to improve the human-computer relationship. 770631120a543f84bc076cad8a8413b9: Glaucoma Diagnosis Using Texture Attributes and Pre-Trained CNN’s Glaucoma is an eye disease that damages the optic nerve causing loss of vision. 9d2c9217784b4ec7c3d0b9ec9615be56: MeHarCEn: A Method for Harmonizing Energy Consumption in Data Centers Controlled and efficient energy consumption is a challenge faced daily by managers of small, medium and large Data Centers. 36693001a921857c5c6a1735e9cf9345: Evaluation of Intel Software Guard Extensions via Emulation By allowing the execution of applications in a fully protected context (i.e., within enclaves), the possibilities for new generations of Intel processors in the x86 family are expanded with the Software Guard Extensions (SGX) extension. 7d2a00ab4d39505d369eb887fc891402: IndoLoR -- An Adaptable Platform for Indoor Localization Location systems have become an increasingly integral part of people's lives. e8101e455c9b88291689e05f5dd720bd: Space-scale theory: concepts and approaches Multi-scale approaches have been widely used in various signal analysis and processing applications, being fundamental in cases where there is no preliminary information about the appropriate observation scale. This work provides a brief review of the main space-scale approaches, as well as their fundamental properties. Humanities; Philosophy
e457e2272d69684c42e943b92d723671: Models for capacity-oriented availability assessment of a private cloud High availability is one of the main requirements of applications that use cloud computing. 872e9d96137ef32bfb9c238d7baa1404: Gang Scheduling Algorithms with Migration Strategies in an MCMCA Environment Over the last decade, the rapid advancement of network, hardware and middleware technologies, as well as the sophistication of software resources, have contributed to the emergence of new computational models. 0184fe58a3547d5c9e14a511cb6c4006: Development of a neuro-fuzzy network for predicting the rectal temperature of broiler chickens The objective of this work was to develop and validate a neuro-fuzzy network, based on the LOLIMOT algorithm, for predicting the rectal temperature of broiler chickens. ce86fe4c1b127fe25a02522d0294af37: A computational model for simulating urban transport systems Currently, the difficulties faced in urban commuting are considered an extremely important problem, especially in large cities. 3d80347d4d69fc5acbdcc8bb7ef395b2: Introduction to General Purpose Programming in Graphics Hardware The Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) was initially developed as hardware intended to increase the efficiency and power of graphics processing for rendering tasks. Today, the GPU presents itself as a versatile processing hardware with high computing power. It has become a real possibility in the search for solutions for processing large volumes of data, either as a complement or as an alternative to the use of multicore CPUs or distributed systems. The use of the GPU in general purpose computations is of special interest, since for several applications, there are still no sequential formulations that are fast enough to be computed. This tutorial aims to allow the reader to identify algorithms and applications that are candidates for parallel approaches on the GPU. To this end, we present the fundamentals and concepts involved in generic purpose programming using graphics hardware without the reader being required to have a priori knowledge of 3D graphics systems or parallel systems. computer science; Humanities; Philosophy
f08643fb28dcf3b615af8d48088e17f2: SWEETS: an Expert Recommendation System applied to a Knowledge Management platform Organizations, with the aim of increasing their degree of competitiveness in the market, are constantly looking for new ways to improve the productivity and quality of the products developed, in addition to reducing costs – which is directly related to the increase in net revenue. In order for these objectives to be achieved, it is essential to fully explore the potential of your employees and the possible relationships that these employees have with each other, that is, finding and sharing tacit knowledge. As tactical knowledge is in people's minds, it is difficult to be formalized and documented, therefore, the ideal would be to identify and recommend the person who has the knowledge. Therefore, this dissertation presents the SWEETS Expert Recommendation System and its implementation in the a.m.i.g.o.s. environment, a knowledge management platform based on concepts focused on social networks. SWEETS was developed in two versions, 1.0 and 2.0. Version 1.0, in a proactive way, brings together people with common specialties, sometimes because of their knowledge (writing profile), sometimes because of their interests (reading profile). Version 2.0 of SWEETS does not act proactively, that is, it is necessary to request a user who is a specialist in a given area, and is based on folksonomy to extract an ontology, which is essential to identify people's specialties more effectively. This ontology is reflected by the co-occurrence of tags (concepts) in relation to items (instances) and is domain independent – ​​the main contribution of this dissertation. The implementation of SWEETS in a.m.i.g.o.s. aims to bring benefits such as: minimizing the communication problem in the corporation, providing an incentive for social knowledge and sharing knowledge; thus providing the company with the most effective use of its employees' knowledge. 4f8feb38c2fee89009b8196cbd620694: A Review on Clustering Combination Several clustering algorithms have been proposed in the literature. The use of different clustering algorithms, or even a single algorithm, can obtain different results when applied to the same set of data. The combination of results, obtained from a classification technique or different techniques, is successfully used to improve the stability or performance of these techniques. Therefore, in recent years there has been a growing interest in the use of combining data groupings. In this work, a review is made of the main cluster combination methods found in the literature. To achieve this, the review begins with a description of the combination problem and an analysis of the objectives commonly adopted by combination methods. Next, the need for diversity in the groups to be combined and methods for measuring it are discussed. A criterion for measuring mutual information between clusters is also defined and examples of its use are presented. The performance of the methods has been compared by several authors in the literature and an analysis of these comparisons is carried out in this work. Physics; Humanities; Philosophy
e376f2d257aa8ba08d5b21cb43ce467a: Combining Interaction Models to Improve Coordination in Multiagent Systems The main contribution of this article is the implementation of a hybrid coordination method based on the combination of previously developed interaction models. Interaction models are based on sharing rewards for learning with multiple agents, in order to interactively discover good quality policies. The exchange of rewards between agents during interaction is a complex task and if carried out inappropriately it can cause delays in learning or even cause unexpected behaviors, making cooperation inefficient and converging on an unsatisfactory policy. Based on these concepts, the hybrid method uses the particularities of each model, reducing possible conflicts between actions with different policy rewards, improving the coordination of agents in reinforcement learning problems. Experimental results show that the hybrid method is capable of accelerating convergence, quickly achieving optimal policies even in large state spaces, surpassing the results of classical reinforcement learning approaches. Humanities; Physics; Philosophy
3b4150b5678d1f5db5fb544daf15a79c: A structural approach to calculate similarity between ontology concepts The problem of compatibility between ontologies is still an open problem. To address this problem, we present the algorithm implemented in the GNoSIS system. Our solution makes use of both syntactic and semantic techniques in a structural approach, facilitating the mapping or alignment between ontologies from different domains. This algorithm uses different similarity functions and calculates the degree of similarity between concepts recursively, calculating the result of the similarity function between two concepts based on the degree of total similarity between concepts that are closely related. A validation of the approach is presented in this paper. Humanities; Philosophy; computer science
5adc5af4f23a1151087706b27ba0d9d6: Application of ART neural networks and texture analysis to classify the state of alteration of mineral aggregates A new approach for identifying the state of alteration of mineral aggregates intended for civil construction works is presented. Such identification is of fundamental importance to avoid failures and the occurrence of premature defects when carrying out works that can be attributed to the quality of the aggregate used in terms of its state of alteration.
